changes.after: Make a link easy to recognize and easy to follow with a keyboard.

before: Links should remain recognizable without requiring a particular color perception. An underline provides a non-color cue. Hover and keyboard focus are different states; a visible focus outline should not depend on moving a pointer.

The base underline remains when no interaction state applies. :active means the link is being activated, not the page currently being viewed. :visited may style some properties for links in history, but browsers deliberately hide visited-state details from scripts to protect privacy. Do not test someone’s browsing history with computed styles or selectors. This task does not grade visited colors.

Keep the link underlined before interaction and add a 3px keyboard-focus outline without removing its href. The supplied HTML stays in index.html; edit the CSS. The checks inspect this small page, not every possible browser or accessibility requirement.
after: An underline helps people recognize a link without having to tell colors apart. Keep this cue before anyone points at the link. A focus outline also helps people find the link while using a keyboard.

`:hover` means a pointer is over the link. `:active` means the link is being activated, not that it leads to the current page. `:visited` can style some properties for links in browsing history, but browsers hide details of that state from scripts to protect privacy.

Keep the link’s `href`, which gives its destination. Use Tab to find the focus outline, then Enter to follow the link. This project checks the underline and focus style; it does not inspect browsing history.

before.question: A designer removes the base underline and relies only on a different link color. What useful cue is lost?
choices: The link’s href is automatically deleted.
A way to recognize the link without distinguishing its color.
The browser can no longer focus links.
before.explanation: Presentation can remove a recognition cue without deleting navigation or focus behavior. Preserve an understandable non-color signal.

after.question: The normal underline is removed and only a different link color remains. What useful clue is lost?
choices: A way to recognize the link without telling colors apart.
The link can no longer receive focus.
after.explanation: The link still works, but it has lost a visible clue that does not rely on color.

project.title: Recognizable link states
project.task: Keep the link underlined and give it a 3-pixel keyboard-focus outline. Keep its destination.
